sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].

The path was a step change, not a straight line: growth ran 104.0% in FY2017 and 64.2% in FY2021, then collapsed to 0.1% in FY2023 before recovering to 16.4% in FY2024 and 10.6% in FY2025 [D36][D218][D311][D358][D406].
The FY2017 loss of $3.45 billion was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the IPO-related RSU performance condition and the CEO award [F32][P74].
The FY2022 reversal, with the operating loss widening 98.7% to $1.40 billion, came as cost of revenue and operating expenses rose faster than revenue [F17][D264][P42].
In FY2025 advertising revenue of $5.19 billion contributed 5.3pp of the 10.6% growth, while Other Revenue of $745 million contributed 5.4pp [S39][S42][D538][D545][D406].

Advertising grew on a roughly 17% increase in impressions, largely from Sponsored Snaps and Spotlight, partly offset by a roughly 10% lower cost per impression; other revenue rose on subscription growth [P24].
North America remains the largest market at 58.6% of revenue but contributed only 4.4pp of FY2025 growth, against 3.7pp from Rest of world at 23.0% of revenue [D456][D458][D497][D499].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth, so revenue grew 5.5pp faster than operating costs [D423][D406][D430].
The net loss narrowed 34.0% while the diluted share count rose 2.1%, so the basic loss per share fell 35.7% to $0.27 [D408][D425][F60][D409].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, far above the -32.4% median and the -422.5% low of FY2017 [F30][D554][D555][D553].
The 5.7pp improvement in FY2025 came from cost of revenue (+1.1pp), R&D (+1.3pp) and other lines (+3.3pp) [D419][D431][D432][D433].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events and lower advertising investment, while R&D rose $101.9 million on product development headcount [P22][P23].
In FY2025 net margin of -7.8% sat 1.2pp above the -9.0% operating margin, helped by $68.9 million of other income that included $96.7 million of debt extinguishment gains [F50][F30][X130][P18].

Operating cash flow of $656.2 million in FY2025 exceeded the $460.5 million net loss, and free cash flow of $437.2 million was a 7.4% margin, the window high against a -4.1% median [F80][F40][F100][D393][D560][D561].
Operating cash flow rose on the net loss adjusted for $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation, $163.6 million of D&A and $96.7 million of debt extinguishment gains [P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A, so capital intensity stays modest [F90][D392][D395].
Cash generation now rests heavily on non-cash add-backs, with stock-based compensation at 155.0% of operating cash flow [D396].

Cash and investments of $2.94 billion against $3.54 billion of debt left net debt of $596 million, or net cash of -10.1% of revenue, against a 45.0% peer median and a 0th percentile rank among five internet peers [D397][D398][D399][D400][D579][D578].
Net cash fell from $1.44 billion in FY2021 to -$205 million in FY2023 and to -$596 million in FY2025 [D211][D304][D399].
Buybacks of $750.9 million in FY2025 were 171.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D401][D402][D425].
The February 2025 refinancing issued $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes and repurchased $1.4 billion of 2026-2028 notes, lifting interest expense by $100.4 million [P1][P2][P19].
Net losses persist in all ten years, from -$514.6 million in FY2016 to -$460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
The loss is narrowing but ten years without a profit year leaves little evidence the model earns its cost of capital [R1].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last nine years [R2][D390].
At 191.1% of the operating loss, compensation is the main reason the GAAP loss overstates cash burn and understates dilution [R2][D404].
Net cash fell for four straight years into net debt of $596 million in FY2025 [R3][D399].
With buybacks at 171.7% of free cash flow, capital return is being funded partly from the shrinking liquidity buffer [R4][D402].
Whether the operating margin holds above the -9.0% FY2025 high or slips back toward the -32.4% median, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D554][D555].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue recovers from -10.1% or extends the four-year decline, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D400][R3].
Whether stock-based compensation stays below the 17.1% of revenue recorded in FY2025, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D390][R2].
